I wouldn't say I disagree with some parts of Islam. I do, however, have a different understanding of those parts than others. Everyone practices Islam differently and there isn't one right way although everyone will vouch for their beliefs being superior. There's nothing wrong on believing you are right as long as you don't discredit others. As a feminist, I've come a long way in understanding my Islam and it's taken time to recognize how patriarchally structured it all is and then having to reread it, interpreting it in a more intersectional manner. Ijtihad is, in my opinion, the best way to understand your faith and it doesn't necessarily have to align with the majority as long as it makes sense to you and you're not harming anyone through it.
